Capture It - Game Features Script

Capture It is a friends-only creative video-making game where players can create, film, and share all kinds of content.

Players can make movies, videos, Shorts, animations, roleplays, and livestreams all within one platform.

The movie editor allows users to build stories scene by scene. Players can choose thumbnails, add sounds, place characters, set poses, adjust camera angles, and fully control how each scene looks and feels.

Filming takes place across a variety of built-in maps such as cities, schools, castles, beaches, and forests. Players also have the ability to build their own maps or copy existing ones and customize them freely.

Capture It includes a wide range of free extensions. These include AI Summaries, the BrightUp Thumbnail Editor, a Video Title Generator, a Thumbnail Tester, additional video assets, and special packs like the Pirate Pack. No Robux is required to access these tools.

Players can enhance their videos using many different assets such as trees, sharks, ocean items, plants, rocks, pirate props, furniture, and visual effects to make each scene more detailed and unique.

Captions can be enabled so viewers can read dialogue and chat clearly, even when audio is not available.

Profiles can be customized with banners, playlists, connected videos, favorite creations, and featured thumbnails to showcase a creator's work.

Videos can be promoted to help reach a larger audience and grow visibility. Promoted videos can be skipped instantly by viewers.

The game also includes copyright protection tools to help safeguard original creations. Reports are reviewed to maintain fairness and support a creative community.

In addition to creation tools, players can enjoy mini games or use special maps as filming locations for their projects.

Capture It is built around creativity, storytelling, and sharing-giving players everything they need to create and express their ideas.

answers.ask: Each built-in set has its own setting - is there a house style tying them together, or should each be built in its own register?
answers.answer: Each set should use its own matching register—city, school, castle, beach, and forest should look distinct—but keep a clean, accessible Roblox creative-tool style across all of them.

answers.ask: Which set should be built first, and should they share one world or be separate places?
answers.answer: Build the city set first, since it is the most flexible starting filming location. Keep the sets as separate selectable places so each can be loaded cleanly for filming.

answers.ask: How large should each filming set be? A set built for camera work is usually smaller than a playable map.
answers.answer: Keep each set compact and built for camera work: a small, dense collection of recognizable filming areas rather than a large explorable map.

scene_prompt: Create a compact, camera-ready city filming set in a clean, accessible Roblox creative-tool style. Build it as a small, dense collection of recognizable urban filming areas with streets, building facades, and flexible open spaces for placing characters, props, and cameras. Keep this city set separate from other selectable built-in filming locations, which include distinct school, castle, beach, and forest sets in their own matching visual registers.
blob:
### Genre
`No Genre`: this is a creative filming environment, not a game mode with a scoring, combat, race, or progression loop. The decided axes are `enclosure` exterior, `verticality` single-surface, and `zone-count` multi-zone because the city, school, castle, beach, and forest are separate selectable filming places. `structure` and `play-space` remain at their defaults.

### Shape and preset
No shape applies under `No Genre`. Use no preset: the requested city is a compact camera set rather than a general explorable-place or social-space layout. The city is the first set to build; its four companion sets remain distinct maps in their own visual registers.

### Config requirements
Use `path-circulation` for short, readable streets and walkways connecting the filming backdrops while leaving clear camera and prop-placement space. Do not add unrequested interiors, residents, water, terrain relief, landmarks, or gameplay hazards.

### Layout requirements
No gameplay volumes, spawners, checkpoints, pickups, or scoring markers are required. The filming workflow and camera controls are not layout placements.

### Layout components
Build one compact city set composed of a central flexible open plaza, two or three short intersecting streets, and dense street-facing building facades around their edges. Make the facades recognizable urban backdrops with varied storefront, apartment, and civic-style fronts, while keeping their ground-level foregrounds uncluttered for character blocking, placed props, and camera angles. Connect every filming area by broad pedestrian-friendly street segments rather than a long traversable city grid. Use flat paved ground with curbs and small modular street dressing that can be moved or avoided during shoots. Frame the compact perimeter with facade walls, corner buildings, and skyline flats so shots read as a city without requiring a large exterior world. Compose the set as several distinct camera-ready vignettes visible from the plaza and streets, with clean sightlines and multiple facing directions.

### Render order
Use `isometric`: visual readability, recognizable facades, and filming compositions lead; no gameplay topology requires plan-first validation.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is small, driven by the requirement for a dense camera-work set rather than an explorable city. Theme is clean, accessible Roblox creative-tool urban styling, distinct from the school, castle, beach, and forest companion sets. Use `P4` because the five named built-in filming sets are separate selectable maps rather than one shared surface.
